themes.label: Boundary Markers (Horoi)
themes.rationale: The inscription is a detailed record of boundary markers (horoi) placed to define the territory between Lacedaemon and Messene.

themes.label: Edicts and Ordinances
themes.rationale: This is an official administrative document recording a boundary survey conducted by a Roman imperial official, a freedman of Vespasian.
themes.quote: Τ. Φλαούιος Σεβαστοῦ Οὐεσπασιανοῦ ἀπελεύθερος Μόνιμιτος χωρομέτρης τοὺς προγεγραμμ νους ὅρους ἀντιβαλὼν ὑπέγραψα

themes.label: Registers and Catalogues
themes.rationale: The text functions as a sequential register of specific boundary points, distances in feet, and marker descriptions.
themes.quote: ὅρος εἰκοστὸς τρίτος ἐτέθη ἐπιγραφὴν ἔχων

themes.label: Treaties and Agreements
themes.rationale: The document settles a territorial dispute and defines the shared border between two political entities, Lacedaemon and Messene.
themes.quote: ὁρίζει γῆν λακεδαιμονίων τε καὶ μεσσηνίων
themes.ambiguity_note: The text records the implementation of a boundary decision rather than the treaty text itself.

themes.label: Other Stone
themes.rationale: The inscription is carved into natural rock (petra).

themes.label: Fragmentary
themes.rationale: The inscription is highly fragmentary with significant portions of the text missing and reconstructed.

rationale: This inscription, dated to 78 AD, records a formal land survey conducted by Titus Flavius Monimitus, a freedman of the Emperor Vespasian. The document delineates the boundary between Lacedaemon (Sparta) and Messene, listing a series of numbered boundary markers (horoi) and providing precise measurements in feet (podes). Many of these markers were inscribed directly onto natural rock (petrai). The text also references local religious landmarks, including the sanctuaries of Zeus Hypsistos and Artemis Limnatis, and mentions the Eleutherolacones league.
